result.title: EMMA: Event-Driven Multimodal Memory System with Multi-Agent Retrieval
result.summary: Long video understanding requires reasoning over hours of content that far exceed the context window of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Existing approaches compress video into fixed-length clips, yet events are fragmented and unrelated content is merged, yielding noisy retrieval. To overcome this challenge, we propose EMMA, an Event-driven Multimodal Memory system with Multi-Agent retrieval, which organizes memory around semantic events in three stages: (1) Event segmentation: a dual-stream detector adaptively locates event boundaries by fusing visual semantic drift with spoken transitions, rather than fixed windows. (2) Memory construction: built on the detected events, a three-level hierarchy of raw video, clip-level memory, and event-level memory stores content at progressively higher semantic abstraction. (3) Memory retrieval: a multi-agent framework collaboratively queries this hierarchy through query decomposition, tiered search, evidence validation, and answer generation, narrowing evidence from coarse events to precise clips. Extensive experiments on three challenging benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements, showing the effectiveness of our event-aligned memory system. Code, prompt templates, and reproduction scripts are available at https://github.com/BAI-LAB/EMMA.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EMMA，一个事件驱动的多模态记忆系统：用融合视觉语义漂移与语音转折的双流检测器自适应切分事件边界，构建原始视频、片段级、事件级三级记忆层级，并以多智能体框架完成查询分解、分层搜索、证据校验与答案生成，用于长视频理解与问答。
AI.relevance_reason: 其粗到细的分层检索与「证据校验」环节可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选及 LOOK/取证据决策提供可核查的方法线索，但论文面向外部视频记忆检索，不涉及 latent 推理状态，需确认校验环节的具体收益。
